Hi Vanessa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement had two follow-ups before we sign the pilot SOW: one technical, one billing. I wanted to capture them in writing so our legal/finance folks can review. High level: we want to understand how token rounding and minimums apply to demo/preview sessions vs committed production calls. Specifics below:

1) Streaming responses: when a chat is streamed to a web demo (user drops in/out), do you bill on the final complete generated token count or on bytes/chunks sent during streaming? If the UI closes before the model finishes, is that truncated output billed?

2) Demo/preview accounts: For our internal demos, we will have many short, interactive sessions (5–15 tokens of input, ~20–80 tokens output). Does Redwood apply a per-request minimum or rounding quantum that would make those tiny sessions expensive relative to real usage?

3) Pilot pricing ask: For the 3-month pilot, can you give a simple worked example of how a day of 200 short demo sessions (avg 60 generated tokens) would be billed with your standard rounding/minimums, and what it would look like with the proposed pilot waiver you mentioned on the call?

Attached: sample session logs (anonymized) from our demo environment. Finance marked this as high priority.

Thanks — appreciate the quick clarification so procurement can move forward.

— Lila

Hi Lila — thanks for writing this up and for the logs — helpful. Quick answers up front, then a short worked example. CC'ing Aditya (billing) and Tessa (customer success) to confirm and sign off.

Short answers:
- Streaming: we bill on the final tokenized output associated with the request id. If a stream is cut early (client disconnect), we bill for tokens generated up to the last committed token. Chunks/packets aren't billed separately.
- Per-request rounding: standard hosted plan applies a rounding quantum of 10 tokens per request for generated tokens (not for input tokens). In other words, generated tokens are rounded up to the nearest 10. Input tokens are billed exactly.
- Demo/preview accounts: for low-volume interactive demos we offer two alternative treatments (pilot-specific):
  1) Waived micro-floor: for the pilot we can waive the 10-token quantum for requests flagged as preview sessions and instead aggregate usage per day and apply a 1,000-token daily floor (rounded up).
  2) Commit credit: if you prefer committed credits, we can convert expected demo usage into a monthly committed bucket with a 25% discount and zero per-request rounding.

Worked example (standard behavior):
- 200 sessions / day
- avg input tokens per session: 8
- avg generated tokens per session: 60 -> rounded up to 60 (already a multiple of 10) -> billed generated tokens = 60 * 200 = 12,000
- billed input tokens = 8 * 200 = 1,600
- total billed tokens = 13,600

If generated avg were 57 tokens, rounding makes each session billed as 60 -> delta +3*200 = +600 tokens/day.

Pilot waiver option (waived quantum + daily aggregate floor):
- Aggregate generated tokens across all preview requests for the day: 57 * 200 = 11,400 generated tokens
- Aggregate input tokens for the day: 1,600
- Apply 1,000-token daily floor only if aggregate generated+input < 1,000 (not the case here), otherwise bill exact aggregate. For days under 1,000 total we charge 1,000.

Net: for your sample logs, rounding impact is small because most sessions are ~60. The waiver protects you for lots of tiny sessions (e.g., 200 sessions at 8 generated tokens each) where rounding would otherwise multiply cost.

Questions for you before Aditya gives final confirmation:
- Do you want per-day aggregation by the preview flag, or by the IP/tenant (i.e., pool all demo sessions across your org)?
- Which model variant will you use in the pilot (gpt-redwood-120b, fast-quantized-30b, etc.)? Model price materially changes the effective delta from rounding.

I'll have Aditya post an explicit invoice-style example with numbers at our model-tier prices.

Best,

Hi all — quick numeric confirmation using our current hosted list rates (gpt-redwood-120b as example):
- list rate generated token = $0.000016/token
- list rate input token = $0.000004/token

Scenario A (standard rounding to 10):
- 200 sessions, avg gen 60, avg input 8 -> generated billed = 12,000 tokens -> $0.192
- input billed = 1,600 tokens -> $0.0064
- total/day = $0.1984 -> monthly (~22 working days) = $4.365

Scenario B (small sessions, heavy rounding): avg gen 8 tokens -> rounded to 10 -> generated billed = 10*200 = 2,000 -> actual = 1,600 (delta 400) -> additional cost/day ~ $0.0064

Pilot concession (recommended): we will: 
- Flag preview sessions via tenant tag and aggregate daily across the tenant.
- Remove per-request 10-token quantum for preview-tagged sessions for the pilot period.
- Apply a monthly pilot-level cap/credit: we will provide a $500 usage credit for preview/demo activity across the 3-month pilot. Any overage billed at 60% of list rate (i.e., 40% pilot discount).

Notes / caveats:
- KV cache reuse: cache hits are not deducted from the generated token count — we only bill emitted tokens. If you rely on heavy prefix reuse, that reduces generated tokens and therefore cost.
- If you open multiple simultaneous streams for the same request id (uncommon in web demo), we still attribute to a single request; partial disconnect behavior above applies.

If that works for Acme, legal can include the preview flag language in the SOW (simple addendum). Tessa — please confirm the operational tag and how to enable it for Acme accounts.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Billing & Product Finance, Redwood Inference
